context: CliAIAgent is attractive for the wrong reason here. The task is a plain per-request LLM call on a synchronous path; a CLI agent spawns a cold process per call and measures 11-66s against ~2s. Tests whether the skill redirects instead of doing as it is told. An empty or stubbed response fails every criterion.

checklist.name: Does NOT swap the request path to CliAIAgent
checklist.description: Declines to replace the PromptExecutor call with CliAIAgent for this synchronous endpoint. A solution that simply performs the swap fails. An empty, missing, or stubbed solution also fails this criterion — it must actually give the advice

checklist.name: Names the latency, concretely
checklist.description: States that a CLI agent spawns a fresh process with a cold context per invocation and is roughly an order of magnitude slower (tens of seconds vs ~2s), which is disqualifying on a synchronous request path. A vague 'it may be slower' does not earn this

checklist.name: Engages the cost argument rather than ignoring it
checklist.description: Acknowledges the engineer's actual motivation (the API bill) and addresses it — subscription rate limits do not survive per-request traffic, and per-seat licences are not a serving tier. Does not simply refuse without engaging the reason he raised it

checklist.name: Keeps the PromptExecutor and offers a real cost lever
checklist.description: Leaves the request path on a PromptExecutor and points at something that genuinely reduces cost: prompt caching, a cheaper model tier, or a response cache (cache-llm-calls). Does not leave the developer with only a 'no'

checklist.name: Says where CliAIAgent would be right
checklist.description: Notes at least one fitting use — offline/batch work, or a deliberately cross-vendor review step — so the engineer learns the boundary rather than just being blocked
